subject: Post-call: EdgeFin performance/SLO benchmark methodology & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@edgefin.com>, Tom Harris <tharris@edgefin.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-24T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Performance/SLO benchmarks & next steps

Hi Alice / Tom — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a reproducible baseline run scheduled:

Recap from call:
- Business goal: GenAI assistant in trading UI; SLOs called out by EdgeFin team (see below).
- Primary concerns: p95 tail latency, throughput at peak concurrency, streaming responsiveness for incremental tokens, and reproducibility of benchmarks across our infra.

EdgeFin targets you mentioned:
- Latency: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms (server-side request completion).
- Throughput: baseline target 200 req/s for mid-traffic windows; burst to 500 req/s for short periods.
- Concurrency: user concurrency target ~8 simultaneous sessions per instance.
- Streaming: support first-token latency < 120ms and sustainable token throughput ~1000 tokens/sec when streaming.

What we can provide now (attached):
- edgefin-benchmark-harness-v1.zip (benchmark harness + runner script)
- edgefin-promptset-v2.json (canonical prompt sets + sample payloads)
- measurement-definitions.md (how we measure p50/p95/p99, first-byte vs token latency)

Proposed methodology (high level):
1) Environment capture: record model version, quantization, instance type, kernel versions.
2) Warm-up: 5 warm-up runs to populate caches (we can disable prefix/KV caching for a fair cold baseline if you prefer).
3) Sampling: 3 independent runs of the full prompt set; aggregate p50/p95/p99 across runs.
4) Streaming: measure two separate metrics — time-to-first-token and sustained token throughput.
5) Reproducibility: fixed seeds, saved payloads, and a run manifest stored in Drive.

Next steps / asks from EdgeFin:
- Confirm the targets above (latency/throughput/concurrency/streaming).
- Provide API key or test token and a small sample dataset (anonymized) so we can run an initial baseline in our Dedicated environment.
- Confirm a convenient time window the week of Jun 28 for us to run a canary scale benchmark (suggest Jun 30 09:00 PT).

If that works I'll loop in engineering to schedule and share the runbook.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: edgefin-benchmark-harness-v1.zip (tooling), edgefin-promptset-v2.json, measurement-definitions.md

From: Tom Harris <tharris@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Wu <alice.wu@edgefin.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance/SLO benchmarks & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and matches what we discussed. A few clarifying questions before we hand over a token and dataset:

1) Measurement windows: when you say p95/p99 are these measured on server-side end-to-end request completion or do you separate first-byte (TTFB) for streaming? We need to be explicit because our product metrics track both.
2) Warm-up / caching: we typically want a realistic warm cache result for production (not cold). Can you run both cold and warm baselines?
3) Reproducibility: how do you handle variability across GPU host kernels / infra? We need repeatable numbers we can compare month-over-month.

We're comfortable with Jun 30 09:00 PT as a canary; we'd prefer a smaller scale canary first (e.g., 50 req/s) to validate configs. Also attaching our SLA/requirements doc (internal).

Can you share the exact measurement-definitions.md you'll use? Also any constraints on streaming protocols (do you support chunked HTTP/2, SSE)?

—Tom
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeFin
tharris@edgefin.com

Attachment stubs: EdgeFin-SLA-requirements.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tharris@edgefin.com>, Alice Wu <alice.wu@edgefin.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-26T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance/SLO benchmarks & next steps

Appreciate the questions — see inline answers and a few clarifications below. I've attached the measurement-definitions.md we'll use and a short runbook excerpt.

1) Measurement windows:
- p50/p95/p99: measured on server-side end-to-end request completion for non-streaming. For streaming we report both time-to-first-token (TTFT) and token-stream throughput (tokens/sec).
- We will include both TTFB and last-token latency in the streaming report so you can map to your product metrics.

2) Warm-up / caching:
- We can run both a cold baseline (prefix/KV caches disabled) and a warm baseline (caches enabled). Our recommendation is to present both so you can trade steady-state vs cold-start economics.
- Warm baseline uses 5 warm-up iterations as noted; each measured run has 3 independent samples.

3) Reproducibility across infra:
- The harness pins model binary, kernel versions, and CUDA/cuDNN when possible; run artifacts include machine image id, driver versions, and the exact runner commit.
- We also save raw traces for a subset of requests and attach the run manifest in Drive so you can re-run against the same config.

Streaming protocols supported:
- Our runtime supports chunked HTTP/1.1 streaming and HTTP/2 streaming (SSE-style token frames). We'll confirm token framing semantics in the harness README.

Canary plan suggestion:
- Phase 1 (canary): Jun 30 09:00 PT — run 50 req/s with streaming enabled to validate protocol and measurement capture.
- Phase 2 (baseline): Jul 1 — run full-scale baseline (200 req/s target, concurrency 8).

What we need from EdgeFin to proceed:
- A short-lived test API key (scoped) and an endpoint URL.
- Sample payloads (5-10 anonymized user prompts) or confirmation to use the attached prompt set.
- Confirmation you're OK with both cold and warm baselines being published in a shared report.

I'll schedule Jun 30 canary and loop engineering on the exact runner. Aditya / Dev — please review the attached runbook and confirm streaming test harness readiness (see checklist in runbook).

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: measurement-definitions.md, runbook-excerpt (in harness zip)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: EF benchmark prep — tasks (HS-123456)

Team — locking in internal tasks ahead of the Jun 30 canary. Short checklist:

- Aditya: validate that the harness supports HTTP/2 streaming framing and that TTFT is captured as a first-class metric (metric name: ttft_ms).
- Priyom: prepare a run manifest template that pins host kernel, driver versions, and model commit; include instructions for saving run artifacts to the shared Drive folder.
- Dev: confirm we can run cold baseline mode (disable KV/prefix caching) and warm baseline mode; automate the 5 warm-up and 3-sample sequence in the runner.
- All: ensure attachments from the vendor (edgefin-promptset-v2.json) are validated against our payload schema; flag any prompt pieces that require truncation to fit token limits.

Deliverables before Jun 29 17:00 PT: run manifest template, updated harness with streaming TTFT metric, and a smoke-test report from a 50 req/s canary run.

I'll coordinate the exact runner window with EdgeFin. HubSpot deal HS-123456 — update stages accordingly after canary results.

Thanks —
Marissa
